Introduce named cache profiles and toolchain containers to shrink CI latency

Problem: CI median full-build time has regressed to ~9m on pushes with cold caches; flaky cache misses on third-party deps and inconsistent base-image layering are the dominant causes. We also see noisy lint/toolchain installs that add 30–90s to many jobs.

Goal: Reduce median CI build time to <= 4m on common change sets by (1) introducing explicit, named cache profiles that normalize layer/layout across repos and CI workers, (2) packaging language toolchains and linters into immutable toolchain containers, and (3) introducing cache-priming heuristics for frequent repos and preflight builders. Success metrics: median build time, 95th percentile job latency, cache hit-rate, and monthly CI spend. Target: median <= 4m, cache hit-rate >= 85% for warm runs, 95th percentile latency reduced by 40%, 20% CI cost reduction on CI bill.

Proposed approach:
- Named cache profiles: define a small set of cache profiles (node-fast, python-build, go-layers, common-runtime) that specify a canonical layer order and named mount points. Repos opt into a profile via CI config (one-line flag). This ensures identical cache keys across workers and reduces invalidation surface.
- Toolchain containers: publish pinned, hermetic containers (toolchain:v1, v2) that include OS packages, language runtimes, linters, formatters, and common native deps. CI tasks use these as base images or sidecar toolchain mounts instead of installing during job runtime.
- Cache priming + heuristics: a lightweight priming controller in our CI fleet will pre-populate popular profiles for active PRs and the default branch. Heuristics prioritize by recent activity, size of dependency changes, and latency sensitivity.
- Lint-as-service: move slow format/lint steps to a reusable, short-lived service that runs once per PR and caches results; optionally gated to run on modified-language files only.
- Observability and migration: ship metrics for cache hit rate, per-layer invalidation counts, toolchain image pull times, and per-job install time. Provide a migration guide and linter rule to opt-in repos detect missing profile.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype named cache profiles and toolchain container for node and python in a canary group (5 repos) — 2 weeks.
2) Measure and expand profiles to go and rust; publish toolchain images to internal registry — 1 week.
3) Enable priming controller for top-20 active repos and run A/B (profile opt-in vs current) — 2 weeks.
4) Gradual rollout to all repos, add lint-as-service, and deprecate per-job installs — 2–3 weeks.

Risks + mitigations:
- Toolchain drift: lock images and add regular rebuild cadence + SBOMs.
- Large image pulls increase network cost: use delta-pushes and regional registries; measure pull times and fall back to install-on-demand if pull fails.
- Repo-specific build idiosyncrasies: keep escape hatch to opt-out and a migration checklist.

Operational notes: this is intentionally low-customer-impact (developer-only CI), but large wins to engineering cycle time. Keep stakeholders: DX, Infra, and Security in sync for image signing and registry policies.

2026-03-01 - Diego Ramos: Triage — collected build traces (CI dashboard) and sampled 200 recent PRs. Root causes largely cache keys + per-job installs. Recommended named cache profiles + toolchain containers as first step.
2026-03-04 - Amaya Chen: Design decision — prefer named profiles over per-repo custom layering to maximize cross-repo cache reuse. Drafted initial profiles: node-fast, python-build. See confluence: /confluence/ci-modern/profiles-draft (placeholder).
2026-03-07 - Amaya Chen: PoC complete for node-fast profile on 3 repos. Warm-run median build dropped from 6m to 2.9m. Cold-run improvement marginal until priming controller was added. Collected artifacts: github.com/redwood/ci-profiles/pull/120
2026-03-10 - Security (Nikhil Patel): Reviewed toolchain container signing requirements. Need image signing (cosign) and SBOMs before broad rollout. Added as blocker for org-wide publish.
2026-03-12 - Diego Ramos: Priming controller prototype reduced cold-run variance — measured 82% cache hit on primed profiles. Created follow-up ticket to integrate with regional registries: ENG-965100.
2026-03-14 - Amaya Chen: In Progress — working on publishing toolchain:v1 with cosign signatures. Preparing migration docs and CI config snippet for repo owners. Next: run A/B for top-20 repos.
